what_it_measured.text: ABSTRACT Aim: To evaluate the efficacy, safety and immunogenicity of semaglutide injection (synthetic) (Test group) compared with the Reference semaglutide injection [Ozempic, (Reference group)] in Indian patients with Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM).

dose.text: Studytreatmentswereadministeredasonce-weeklysubcutaneous injections using an identical dose- escalation regimen to ensure comparabilitybetweentreatmentgroups.Allrandomisedpatients initiated treatment at Week 0 with semaglutide administered at a dose of 0.25mg once weekly for the first 4weeks.

route.text: Therefore, Sun Pharma has developed a synthetic formulation of semaglutide injection.
Semaglutide, a long-acting GLP-1 RA, is approved in many countries, including India, as a once-weekly subcutaneous injection for significantly improving glycaemic control in adults with T2DM.
The allowance of multiple injection sites is standard for subcutaneous GLP-1 receptor agonists, such as semaglutide, to promote patient convenience, adherence and comfort.

endpoint.text: Secondary endpoints included changes in fasting and post-prandial blood glucose, bodyweight and HbA1c < 7.0% achievers, safety and immunogenicity.
The primary endpoint was change in HbA1c from baseline to Week 24.
The primary efficacy endpoint was the change from baseline in HbA1c to Week 24.

reported_results.text: The leastsquares mean difference (Test-Reference) was −0.09% (95% CI: −0.26 to 0.09), meeting the pre-specified non-inferiority criterion.
At Week 24, both treatments produced significant and comparable reductions in HbA1c (Test: −2.04%, Reference: −1.95%; p < 0.0001 within groups).

The estimated least- squares mean difference between treatments was −0.09%, with a two- sided 95%CIof−0.26%to0.09%.TheupperboundoftheCIwasbelow the predefined non- inferiority margin of 0.4%, thereby demonstrating non- inferiority of the Test to the Reference semaglutide injection.
3 | Results 3.1 | Patient Disposition A total of 465 patients were screened, of whom 314 were randomised to receive either the Test semaglutide or Reference semaglutide injection.
The change from baseline in both groups at Week 24 was statistically significant (p < 0.0001 each).
